subject: regw
note: Open questions of the Regulation W transactions encoding (covered transactions, limits, collateral, low-quality assets, valuation and exemptions), row transactions-2026-11, recorded 2026-11-28 from NOTES.md (‘Forks and open questions’, ‘The independent test pass’) and independent-readings-b.md. Eighteen entries, all open: no domain expert has read this encoding against Part 223, so none is a legal ruling. Where NOTES.md states a default as the encoder's own, taken.rationale carries the label ‘decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review’, the date being that of the commit that wrote the NOTES.md paragraph. F1 is a switch: an enumerated input the caller supplies, both constructors execute, and the tests assert both; the code writes no default, and the default named is the first constructor of the declaration. It is recorded as delegated-to-fact with the field named, because the register's interpretation-field arm requires a TYPICALLY default and this module has none. F7 to F9 are not forks between two readings of the words: they record rules that are in force and that the encoding does not apply, or that the independent test pass had no interface to test, with the way the code answers as the taken reading; the second reading of each is the encoder's description of the rule the encoding does not apply, drawn from the provision, and NOTES.md does not state it. Reading ids are camel-case names; the exact constructor name is given in the description. Witness line numbers are lines of the .l4 files at the commit that deposited this register. The questions about the affiliate definition (the four switches of the record `Readings`, cross-holdings, groups of shareholders and the fiduciary rules) are in the register of affiliates-2026-11; this row holds byte copies of those modules (NOTES.md, ‘Copied modules’) and does not repeat them. F10 to F18 were added on 2026-11-28 after a review found them in independent-readings-b.md (R1, R3, R5, R8 to R10) or in NOTES.md and not entered; F13 is about what an output field means more than about the text, and the second reading of F16 is the register writer's. Not entered, and recorded in NOTES.md and independent-readings-b.md instead: R6 (nothing turns on it in an assessment, as NOTES.md says), R11 (slice A's switch passed through), IA1 to IA14, and the NOTES.md paragraphs on the principal amount of a revolving credit facility, collateral and a partial exemption, what the assessment takes from the caller, the dates in 223.42(n) and (o), and the conventions of the encoding; the NOTES.md pointer sentence names them.

site.anchor: `share is within the five percent allowance`

source.quote: The participating member bank's share of the renewal or extension of additional credit does not exceed its proportional share of the original transaction by more than 5 percent, unless the member bank obtains the prior written approval of its appropriate Federal banking agency

readings.description: Constructor `Five percentage points above the proportional share`. “by more than 5 percent” means five percentage points of the transaction above the proportional share: with a proportional share of 25 percent, a share up to 30 is allowed.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.15(b)(3): “does not exceed its proportional share of the original transaction by more than 5 percent”

readings.description: Constructor `Five percent more than the proportional share`. “by more than 5 percent” means five percent more than the proportional share itself: with a proportional share of 25 percent, a share up to 26.25 is allowed.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.15(b)(3): “does not exceed its proportional share of the original transaction by more than 5 percent”

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review. The default is the first constructor of `Five percent reading` (regwb-nouns.l4, line 121); the code writes no default, and the caller supplies the choice in `Asset purchase facts`.

witnesses: regwb-independent-tests.l4 lines 1482-1487 (R2): a share of 25 against a proportional 20 is within the allowance under `pp` and not under `rel`; 21.01 against 20 likewise; 5 against 0 likewise
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph on 223.15(b)(3) “by more than 5 percent” (a switch); independent-readings-b.md R2. The code for 223.15 is in this row.
A switch: an enumerated input supplied by the caller; both constructors execute and the tests assert both.

site.anchor: `amount of the transaction secured by collateral`

source.quote: The loan satisfies the collateral requirements of this section because $500 of the loan is 100 percent secured by obligations of the United States, $400 of the loan is 120 percent secured by debt instruments, and $100 of the loan is 130 percent secured by real estate.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(b)(1): “must be secured by collateral having a market value equal to at least:”

readings.description: Each item of eligible collateral secures its effective value divided by its percentage, and the items together secure the sum, which is compared with the amount to be secured. In the printed example $500 of Treasuries secure $500, $480 of debt securities secure $400 and $130 of real estate secure $100 of a $1,000 loan.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(b)(2): “The loan satisfies the collateral requirements of this section because $500 of the loan is 100 percent secured by obligations of the United States, $400 of the loan is 120 percent secured by debt instruments, and $100 of the loan is 130 percent secured by real estate.”

readings.description: The text states no general rule for combining several kinds of collateral, only the printed example, so how any other combination counts is not decided by the text.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(b)(1): “must be secured by collateral having a market value equal to at least:”

readings.foreclosure: The encoding has to answer for every combination, so it generalises the example; the generalisation is the encoder's reading of the example and not a sentence of the text (NOTES.md).

taken.rationale: The text does not state the general rule, only the example, so this is the reading of it (NOTES.md, the paragraph ‘223.14(b)(2): combining several kinds of collateral’).

notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘223.14(b)(2): combining several kinds of collateral’.

NOTES.md names no rival general rule, so the second reading is the absence of one, in NOTES.md's words. The tests assert the printed example (regwb-collateral-tests.l4, section ‘223.14(b)(2): the printed example’); no rival rule is encoded, so none is tested.

source.quote: A member bank must maintain a security interest in collateral required by this section that is perfected and enforceable under applicable law, including in the event of default resulting from bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation, or similar circumstances.

readings.description: 223.14(c) lists no perfection condition, so an unperfected interest does not change eligibility: `is eligible collateral` is TRUE for an unperfected Treasury and `effective value of collateral` is 0.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(d)(1): “A member bank must maintain a security interest in collateral required by this section that is perfected and enforceable under applicable law, including in the event of default resulting from bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation, or similar circumstances.”

readings.description: Perfection is part of eligibility: `is eligible collateral` is FALSE for an unperfected interest and `effective value of collateral` ignores perfection (it is the market value).

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(d)(1): “A member bank must maintain a security interest in collateral required by this section that is perfected and enforceable under applicable law, including in the event of default resulting from bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation, or similar circumstances.”

readings.description: Both are affected: `is eligible collateral` is FALSE for an unperfected interest and `effective value of collateral` is 0.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(d)(1): “A member bank must maintain a security interest in collateral required by this section that is perfected and enforceable under applicable law, including in the event of default resulting from bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation, or similar circumstances.”

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: the text states the duty to maintain a perfected and enforceable interest and does not say how an imperfect one is valued; the encoding gives such collateral no effective value (NOTES.md).

notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph on 223.14(d)(1), collateral whose security interest is not perfected; independent-readings-b.md R4.

The readings file says that at the level of the amount secured, the requirement being met and the assessment, all three readings treat an unperfected interest as securing nothing; they differ in the answers of `is eligible collateral` and `effective value of collateral` alone. No input on which the three readings differ in an assessment was searched for, so the divergence is not assessed.

source.quote: Aggregate amount of covered transactions means the amount of the covered transaction about to be engaged in added to the current amount of all outstanding covered transactions.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.41: “The following transactions are not subject to the quantitative limits of §§ 223.11 and 223.12”
12 CFR 223.42(c)(2): “The value of the covered transaction is $50.”

readings.description: The part of a transaction an exemption removes (`value exempt`) is not itself counted among the outstanding covered transactions, and does not count toward the limits or the collateral requirement. The outstanding amounts are stated by the caller.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.42(c)(2): “The value of the covered transaction is $50.”

readings.description: An exempt transaction is itself one of “all outstanding covered transactions”, so its whole amount counts in the aggregate amount of 223.3(a).

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(a): “Aggregate amount of covered transactions means the amount of the covered transaction about to be engaged in added to the current amount of all outstanding covered transactions.”

readings.foreclosure: The 223.42(c) example values the covered transaction at the unsecured $50 of a $100 loan, so the printed example does not count the exempt part (NOTES.md).

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: the text does not say whether an exempt transaction is itself counted among the outstanding covered transactions; the 223.42(c) example values the covered transaction at the unsecured $50 of a $100 loan, so the exempt part is not counted. The outstanding amounts are stated by the caller (NOTES.md).

notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘Do exempt transactions count toward the aggregate amount?’. Related: F5, the part of a transaction that an exemption does not remove.

The outstanding amounts the caller states are `Situation`'s `outstanding covered transactions with this affiliate` and `outstanding covered transactions with all affiliates` (regwb-nouns.l4, lines 161-162); the code does not decide whether an exempt transaction belongs in them.

The tests state the outstanding amounts as plain numbers; a search of the row's test files for lines naming both outstanding and exempt found only the comment on the `Situation` signature and comments on scenarios 63 and 64 and on R8 of the independent file, none of which asks whether an exempt transaction belongs among the outstanding amounts, so the divergence is not assessed.

source.quote: Engaging in a credit transaction with an affiliate to the extent that the transaction is and remains secured by:

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.42: “The following transactions are not subject to the quantitative limits of §§ 223.11 and 223.12, the collateral requirements of § 223.14, or the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”
12 CFR 223.42(c)(2): “The value of the covered transaction is $50.”

readings.description: The part an exemption does not remove is not exempt: the limits and the collateral requirements apply to it in full, whichever exemption removed the rest. A loan of 100 with Treasuries of 50 has 50 that counts, and 50 is tested against 10 percent of capital stock and surplus.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.42(c): “Engaging in a credit transaction with an affiliate to the extent that the transaction is and remains secured by:”
12 CFR 223.42(c)(2): “The value of the covered transaction is $50.”

readings.description: Claiming a 223.42 exemption switches the limits and the collateral requirement off for the whole transaction, so “not subject to the quantitative limits” leaves nothing of it to test.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.42: “The following transactions are not subject to the quantitative limits of §§ 223.11 and 223.12, the collateral requirements of § 223.14, or the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”

readings.foreclosure: 223.42(c) exempts a credit transaction only “to the extent that” it is secured by the listed collateral, so a claim cannot reach the part that is not (independent-readings-b.md R7). An earlier version of the encoding switched the limits off for the whole transaction while still reporting the remainder; the independent test pass found it and it was changed (NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’, D2).

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: the part an exemption does not remove is not exempt, so the limits and the collateral requirements apply to it in full, whichever exemption removed the rest (NOTES.md). The family claimed decides only what the exempt part still owes (`requirement still applies`).

witnesses: regwb-independent-tests.l4 lines 1503-1516 (R7), scenarios 66 and 67: a loan of 100 under 223.42(c) with Treasuries of 50; the remaining 50 is not a breach at capital stock and surplus 500 and is a breach at 499; on the other reading neither scenario breaches (independent-readings-b.md R7)
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘A transaction that is exempt in part’; independent-readings-b.md R7. Related: F4, whether an exempt transaction counts among the outstanding covered transactions.

source.quote: The transactions are, however, subject to the safety and soundness requirement of § 223.13 and the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.42: “The following transactions are not subject to the quantitative limits of §§ 223.11 and 223.12, the collateral requirements of § 223.14, or the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”
12 CFR 223.41(c): “Purchasing a loan on a nonrecourse basis from an affiliated depository institution”
12 CFR 223.42(k): “Purchasing from an affiliate, on a nonrecourse basis, an extension of credit”

readings.description: The exemptions are cumulative: a purchase that fits both stays subject to the low-quality asset prohibition of 223.15, because 223.41 says so.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.41: “The transactions are, however, subject to the safety and soundness requirement of § 223.13 and the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”

readings.description: The more favourable exemption applies: a purchase that fits both is not subject to 223.15, because 223.42 says it is “not subject to” it.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.42: “The following transactions are not subject to the quantitative limits of §§ 223.11 and 223.12, the collateral requirements of § 223.14, or the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”

readings.description: The encoding does not choose. The exemption claimed is one stated input (`Exemption claimed`), so the caller names the family and that family's lead-in decides.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.41: “The transactions are, however, subject to the safety and soundness requirement of § 223.13 and the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”

12 CFR 223.42: “The following transactions are not subject to the quantitative limits of §§ 223.11 and 223.12, the collateral requirements of § 223.14, or the prohibition on the purchase of a low-quality asset of § 223.15.”

taken.rationale: The text does not say whether the exemptions are cumulative or whether the more favourable one applies; the encoding takes the exemption family as one stated input, and there is no default for a purchase that fits both (NOTES.md; open, not decided).

witnesses: regwb-assessment-tests.l4 lines 153-156: the same purchase of a past-due asset is a prohibited purchase of a low-quality asset under `An exemption under 223.41` and is not, and may be entered into, under `An exemption under 223.42`
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘A transaction that meets a 223.41 exemption and a 223.42 exemption’ (marked open in NOTES.md).

223.41(c) exempts the purchase of a loan on a nonrecourse basis from an affiliated depository institution; 223.42(k) exempts the purchase of an extension of credit from an affiliate on a nonrecourse basis, on conditions; one purchase can satisfy both.

The encoding takes one exemption family per assessment, so no fixture is a purchase that meets both; the tests give the two lead-ins' answers on one past-due purchase, which is the difference the first two readings turn on.

source.quote: A credit transaction with a nonaffiliate becomes a covered transaction at the time that the nonaffiliate becomes an affiliate of the member bank.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.22(b)(2): “the asset purchase becomes a covered transaction at the time that the nonaffiliate becomes an affiliate of the member bank”
12 CFR 223.23(b)(2): “must be treated according to the same transition rules that apply to credit transactions described in paragraph (b)(2) of § 223.21”

readings.description: Each function answers for one instant, from the facts stated to it. When a transaction became a covered transaction, and how its value moved since, are inputs and not computed. Only the `held` flag of `value of an asset purchase later` (223.22(b)(1)) is reached.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.21(b)(2)(i): “A credit transaction with a nonaffiliate becomes a covered transaction at the time that the nonaffiliate becomes an affiliate of the member bank.”

readings.description: The timing and sequence rules are applied. A credit transaction with a nonaffiliate that becomes an affiliate counts as a covered transaction from that time, and its amount is counted in the aggregate amount for future covered transactions without a required reduction, with the collateral requirement applying promptly if the change comes within a year (223.21(b)(2)(i)). Only where the transaction was made in contemplation of the nonaffiliate becoming an affiliate are the limits and the collateral requirement tested at that time (223.21(b)(2)(ii)). A purchase of an asset or of a security is treated by the matching rules (223.22(b)(2), 223.23(b)(2)).

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.21(b)(2)(i): “A credit transaction with a nonaffiliate becomes a covered transaction at the time that the nonaffiliate becomes an affiliate of the member bank.”
12 CFR 223.22(b)(2): “the asset purchase becomes a covered transaction at the time that the nonaffiliate becomes an affiliate of the member bank”
12 CFR 223.23(b)(2): “must be treated according to the same transition rules that apply to credit transactions described in paragraph (b)(2) of § 223.21”

taken.rationale: NOT MODELLED. The sequence rule of 223.21(b)(2) and the matching rules of 223.22(b)(2) and 223.23(b)(2) are out of scope as a separate phase (NOTES.md, ‘Scope’ and the coverage table). The independent test author had no function to test the timing rules against (NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’; independent-readings-b.md IA13).

notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’ has no paragraph on this; the sources are NOTES.md ‘Scope’, its coverage table row for 223.21(b), 223.22(b)(2) and 223.23(b)(2), and ‘The independent test pass’ (the timing rules of 223.21(b), 223.22(b) and 223.23(b) could not be tested).
One entry covers both lists: the sequences the encoding does not model (223.21(b), 223.22(b)(2), 223.23(b)(2)) and the timing rules the independent pass could not test are the same provisions.
Not a fork between two readings of the words: it is recorded because the rules are in force and the encoding does not apply them. The site is the header comment that says so.

source.quote: A member bank must ensure that any required collateral that subsequently is retired or amortized is replaced with additional eligible collateral as needed to keep the percentage of the collateral value relative to the amount of the outstanding credit transaction equal to the minimum percentage required at the inception of the transaction.

readings.description: The replacement requirement is the same collateral test run again with the present values: at one instant, keeping up the percentage the collateral stood at when the transaction began is this same test. How the collateral came to be retired is not encoded.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(e): “A member bank must ensure that any required collateral that subsequently is retired or amortized is replaced with additional eligible collateral as needed to keep the percentage of the collateral value relative to the amount of the outstanding credit transaction equal to the minimum percentage required at the inception of the transaction.”

readings.description: The requirement is a duty that runs from the transaction's inception: collateral that is retired or amortized must be replaced, so the rule would need the inception percentage and the history of retirements.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.14(e): “A member bank must ensure that any required collateral that subsequently is retired or amortized is replaced with additional eligible collateral as needed to keep the percentage of the collateral value relative to the amount of the outstanding credit transaction equal to the minimum percentage required at the inception of the transaction.”

taken.rationale: NOT MODELLED beyond one instant: the function answers from the market values stated to it (regwb-collateral.l4, header comment, lines 5-8; NOTES.md coverage table, row 223.14). The independent test author had no function for 223.14(e) to test (NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’; independent-readings-b.md IA13).

source.quote: a member bank must compute compliance on a monthly basis, based on cardholder purchases that were financed by the credit card during the preceding 12 calendar months

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.16(c)(4)(iii): “If a credit card has qualified as a general purpose credit card for 3 consecutive months but then ceases to qualify in the following month, the member bank may continue to treat the credit card as a general purpose credit card for such month and three additional months (or such longer period as may be permitted by the Board)”

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.16(c)(4)(iii): “a member bank must compute compliance on a monthly basis, based on cardholder purchases that were financed by the credit card during the preceding 12 calendar months”

source.quote: The acceptance of a security issued by the affiliate as collateral for an extension of credit to any person or company

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(h)(5): “The issuance of a guarantee, acceptance, or letter of credit, including an endorsement or standby letter of credit, on behalf of the affiliate”

readings.description: The affiliate is the `affiliate concerned`: the issuer in (h)(4), the company on whose behalf in (h)(5), the affiliate party in a netting arrangement. `with` is the counterparty and may be a nonaffiliate. So (h)(4), (h)(5) and netting with a nonaffiliate counterparty are covered, and (h)(4) with a nonaffiliate's security and an affiliate borrower is not.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(h)(4): “The acceptance of a security issued by the affiliate as collateral for an extension of credit to any person or company”
12 CFR 223.3(h)(5): “The issuance of a guarantee, acceptance, or letter of credit, including an endorsement or standby letter of credit, on behalf of the affiliate”

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(h)(4): “The acceptance of a security issued by the affiliate as collateral for an extension of credit to any person or company”

taken.rationale: The text does not say which of the interface's two names 223.3(h) tests; the encoding tests the `affiliate concerned` (independent-readings-b.md R1; NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’, lists R1 among the readings already answered the way the author took them).

site.anchor: `value of credit secured partly by affiliate securities`

source.quote: The total value of the extension of credit less the fair market value of the nonaffiliate collateral

source.quote: any affiliate if the aggregate amount of the member bank's covered transactions with all affiliates would exceed 20 percent of the capital stock and surplus of the member bank

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.11: “(other than a financial subsidiary of the member bank)”

readings.description: 223.11 carves out a financial subsidiary and 223.12 has no such words (“any affiliate”, “all affiliates”): a loan to a financial subsidiary counts toward the 20 percent limit and not toward the 10 percent limit.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.12: “any affiliate if the aggregate amount of the member bank's covered transactions with all affiliates would exceed 20 percent of the capital stock and surplus of the member bank”
12 CFR 223.11: “(other than a financial subsidiary of the member bank)”

readings.description: The carve-out of 223.11 is read into 223.12 as well, so a loan to a financial subsidiary counts toward neither limit.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.11: “(other than a financial subsidiary of the member bank)”

readings.foreclosure: 223.12 has no such words: “any affiliate”, “all affiliates” (NOTES.md).

taken.rationale: The words as printed (NOTES.md, the paragraph ‘223.12 and a financial subsidiary’): 223.2(a)(8) makes a financial subsidiary an affiliate, so the encoding counts a loan to one toward the 20 percent limit and not toward the 10 percent limit.

notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘223.12 and a financial subsidiary (the words as printed)’.
